newsitem.title: USA: EIS International faces another lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: EIS International faces another lawsuit.

text.p: The law firms of Rabin & Peckel LLP and Schacter & Noble PC said on Thursday they commenced a class action suit alleging that EIS International Inc misled investors.

The lawsuit alleges that EIS and several named individuals issued misleading statements about expected revenue and earnings for the third and fourth quarter of 1996. The company also was accused of issuing misleading statements on other matters, including the potential market for its Surefind division.
As a result, the complaint alleges, the EIS share price was artificially inflated, enabling some of the defendants to unload millions of dollars worth of company stock.
The lawsuit purports to represent people who bought EIS shares from May 13, 1996 through March 31, 1997.
A separate class-action lawsuit was filed by two other law firms on April 29, also accusing EIS of misleading investors.
EIS, based in Stamford, Conn., makes phone call processing systems. Its shares were trading up 3/8 to 6-1/2 in afternoon trading on Thursday. Their 52-week high was 31-5/8.
